history.heading: Kingdoms and trade
paragraphs: The territory of Ivory Coast (Côte d'Ivoire) was home to many peoples, including the Akan groups in the east, such as the Baoulé and the Abron, the Kru in the southwest, the Mandé and the Senufo in the north. The northern town of Kong was a centre of Islamic learning and trade, and Akan kingdoms traded gold.
European traders arrived in the 15th century and named the coast after the ivory trade.

history.heading: French colony
paragraphs: France made Ivory Coast a colony in 1893 and part of French West Africa. Plantation agriculture, especially coffee and cocoa, developed using forced labour until 1946. Félix Houphouët-Boigny, a planter and politician, led the movement for rights and self-government.

history.heading: Independence and crises
paragraphs: Ivory Coast became independent on 7 August 1960 with Houphouët-Boigny as president. He ruled until his death in 1993, overseeing the "Ivorian miracle" of growth based on cocoa and coffee, and built a huge basilica in Yamoussoukro, which became the capital.

After his death, disputes over national identity ("Ivoirité"), which excluded northerners, led to a coup in 1999 and a civil war from 2002 that split the country between the north and south. A disputed election in 2010 led to a second conflict in 2011 that killed about 3,000 people, ending when Laurent Gbagbo was arrested and Alassane Ouattara took office.

culture.heading: Peoples and arts
paragraphs: Ivory Coast has more than 60 ethnic groups. French is the official language; Dioula is widely used as a trade language. Islam (mainly in the north) and Christianity (mainly in the south) are the main religions, alongside traditional beliefs.

Ivorian culture is known for masks of the Dan, Baoulé and Senufo peoples, and for popular music genres such as zouglou and coupé-décalé. Attiéké (fermented cassava couscous) with grilled fish and foutou are popular dishes. Football is a passion; the national team won the Africa Cup of Nations in 1992, 2015 and 2024, and Didier Drogba is a national hero.

politics.heading: Presidential republic
paragraphs: Ivory Coast is a presidential republic. Alassane Ouattara has been president since 2011; a 2016 constitution, which he says reset term limits, allowed him to run again in 2020 and 2025. Major opposition candidates were excluded from the 2025 election, which he won. Abidjan is the economic capital and largest city, while Yamoussoukro is the official capital.

economy.heading: Cocoa and growth
paragraphs: Ivory Coast is the world's largest cocoa producer, supplying around 40 percent of global production, and a major producer of cashew nuts, coffee, rubber and palm oil. It also has growing oil, gas and gold production.

It has been one of Africa's fastest-growing economies since 2012, with large investments in infrastructure. Challenges include poverty, inequality, child labour on cocoa farms and deforestation. The currency is the West African CFA franc.
